chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man who had a nosebleed and cleared it by blowing, so some of that blood became small pieces and hit his water container. Is it valid for him to perform wudu from it? He said: If there is nothing apparent in the water, there is no problem; but if there is something apparent, he should not perform wudu from it.
He said: And I asked him about a man who had a nosebleed while he was performing wudu, so a drop dripped into his water container. Is the wudu valid from it? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: Does a nosebleed invalidate wudu if blood mixes with the water?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between minor impurity (najāsah khafīfah) and major impurity in water used for wudu, emphasizing the criterion of visible discernibility (istibān) for blood fragments. It further establishes that direct contamination during the act of wudu invalidates the ritual, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the state of the water at the moment of use determines validity. This ruling underscores the practical application of purity laws in daily worship, ensuring that ritual cleanliness is maintained without undue hardship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about a man with nose bleed, so he cleared it by blowing, so some of that blood came to be in small pieces and hit a water container. Is it correct for him to perform Ablution (Wudhu) from it?’ So heasws said: ‘If there does not happen to be anything which is apparent in the water, so there is no problem; but if there was something apparent, so he should not perform Ablution (Wudhu) from it’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about a man with nose bleed, and he is performing Ablution (Wudhu), so a drop drops into his water container. Is it correct to do the Ablution (Wudhu) from it?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 16. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of one who had a nosebleed; then he blew his nose and parts of it became small segments which came in contact with his water container. Can he take Wudu’ with such water? He (the Imam) said, ’If nothing is visible in the water container it is not harmful. However, if things show in it he must not use it for Wudu’.

5 I (the narrator) then asked him (the Imam) about a man who has nosebleed while taking Wudu’ and a drop falls in his water container. Can he take Wudu 5 with such water? He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot take Wudu’ with such water.’”
